newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge bought 2.1 million of own shares.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge bought 2.1 million of own shares.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp said Thursday it spent more than $150 million this year through April 9 to purchase 2.1 million of its common shares.

"In addition, we invested more than $120 million in capital expenditures during the first quarter," the company said. "Our most notable growth initiative currently is the expansion of our Candelaria copper mine in Chile, where we expect to begin additional production by early 1998."
Capital outlays for Phelps Dodge Mining Co during the latest quarter were $94.5 million, including $47.3 million for the expansion of Candelaria mining operations.
Capital outlays were $27.3 million for Phelps Dodge Industries.
The company said capital outlays in the corresponding 1996 period were $65.4 million for Phelps Dodge Mining and $33.2 million for Phelps Dodge Industries.
Phelps Dodge said it expects 1997 capital outlays to be about $500 million for Phelps Dodge Mining, including $175 million for Candelaria expansion, and $200 million for Phelps Dodge Industries.
Through April 9, the company said, it had purchased a total of 9,062,000 common shares at a cost of $585.4 million under the share purchase authorization granted in 1995.
This left 938,000 shares authorized for purchase.
There were 63,438,000 common shares outstanding on March 31, it added. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
